observation.visible_scene: A close, static view of a smoldering pile of charred debris (dark, matted burnt vegetation/leaf litter mixed with ash and pale fragments). A thick column of white-grey smoke rises and billows from the center and left of the pile, drifting upward. On the right edge of the pile a small open flame burns continuously, with a vertical post at the far left and scattered pipes/wood and ash in the blurred background. The scene is a fire/smoke event already in progress at both crop boundaries.
visible_changes: The white smoke plume from the center-left continuously rises, thickens, thins, and shifts its shape and horizontal spread from frame to frame, indicating ongoing smoldering and air movement.

The small flame on the right flickers: its height, width, and outline change each frame, at times splitting into two tongues (e.g. frames 16-17) and at times showing a brief separate ember/spark just above it (e.g. frames 4, 16, 20).
The flame persists throughout the entire excerpt without going out; its base location on the right side of the pile stays fixed while only its luminous shape deforms.
The charred pile, the left vertical post, and the background debris remain in fixed positions (no object translation); the only motion is the smoke and flame dynamics.
No camera pan/zoom is evident; framing of the pile and background stays constant across frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the pile and when the fire began or will end.
The exact material composition of the burnt pile and the background objects.
Whether the smoke and flame are produced by the same burning mass or by separate smoldering spots.
Events before t=0 and after t=3.2s (the clip is a temporal crop, not a complete burn).
uncertain_details: Whether the small ember above the flame in some frames is a detached spark or part of the same flame tongue.
Whether the apparent drift of the smoke includes any wind direction change versus camera-independent turbulence.
Identity of the pale fragments in the pile (ash vs. unburnt material).
